after: ## Transport, travel and tourism as a source of issues
alt: Rings for road safety: locally, parents in the fictional town of Benmoor want a crossing; nationally, speed limits and motorbike rules; globally, the WHO 2023 estimate of about 1.19 million road deaths a year, down 5% since 2010, the leading cause of death for ages 5 to 29, mostly in low- and middle-income countries. The WHO data is credible but an estimate.
caption: A crossing helps one school; the wider problem needs national action too.

after: ## Perspectives: who sees transport and tourism differently, and why
alt: Timeline: Stockholm trialled a congestion charge from January to July 2006, held referendums in September 2006 and made the charge permanent in August 2007. City voters said 53% yes; surrounding areas about 40% yes. City residents gained quieter streets; many outside drove in and would pay. Traffic fell about 20 to 25%, and a 2012 study found the fall lasted.
caption: Where people live shaped how they voted on the same charge.

alt: Two causes, cheaper flights and cruise calls and social media fame for a few spots, lead to consequences at four levels: a resident struggling through crowds, homes becoming holiday lets as rents rise and families leave, higher tax income but higher costs nationally, and more emissions globally.
caption: One crowded street links to housing, public budgets and global emissions.

alt: Venice charged day-trippers 5 euros on 29 days from 25 April 2024, and in 2025 on 54 days at 5 or 10 euros depending on booking time. The fee targets short-term crowding and gathers data, but protesters argued it does not tackle the long-term problem of residents leaving over housing costs.
caption: An action can fix a short-term problem and miss a long-term one.

alt: For the fictional Kerrow Island, summer-weekend cars on the causeway fell from 5,400 to 4,050 (25%) after a shuttle bus started, suggesting modal shift unless weather or visitor numbers differed. A hoteliers’ association claims most visitors oppose the shuttle, but only 15% of members replied, they reported guests’ views second-hand, and they have a vested interest. A random visitor survey would test it.
caption: Measured counts and second-hand opinions need different checks.

after: ## Courses of action and their effects
alt: France banned some domestic flights from May 2023 where a train takes under two and a half hours, in practice three routes from Paris-Orly; the government called it climate policy while an airline group called it symbolic. Bhutan’s daily visitor fee rose from 65 to 200 US dollars in September 2022, then was cut to 100 dollars from September 2023 when visitor numbers did not recover.
caption: Say how success will be measured, because actions can be adjusted once effects are clear.
